_date: DERIVED from the level number — see game/calendar.ts. Shift 3 is Friday 5 March (night).
_verdict_mode: Pass, Warning or Fine. One warning before a fine, always.
_teaching: Lighting, at night, when it is the brightest thing on the street. Plus the first bribe, and the same bins that were legal on Wednesday now being a finding on Friday.
briefing: Friday, and you are running it after dark. Seasonal lighting goes live today — the window closed on 31 January. Containers are NOT within the window on a Friday.
_cameos: Named residents pinned to addresses rather than rolled. Anything not pinned stays random, so the street is still mostly strangers.
_ambient_animals: The animals loose in yards on this shift. Nights are the wild ones; days are the neighbourhood cat.
story: Friday, and dark by the time you start. The Board schedules these. Nobody has explained why.
Article VIII from today: seasonal lighting comes down by 31 January. It is March.
You will be offered things on this round. What you do about that is between you and the Board.

bounty._character: PINNED, unlike the Poop Bandit. A face drawn at random is a face you have to match; this one is the only person crossing a lawn after dark, and the notice is there to tell you what that means rather than to be searched.
bounty.headline: Reported
bounty.name: Thief
bounty.label: Person matching the report

event._when: Fires when the lights are MARKED and before anything is stamped, so it is the player noticing that summons it rather than the lot being loaded.
event.speaker: The owner, on the porch
event.body: "Forty dollars. Come on. They’re coming down Saturday, my brother-in-law has the ladder. Nobody is hurt by a string of lights in March."

options.label: Take the $40
options.reply: He counts it out twice. The lights stay up, and your pad no longer says they were ever there.

options.label: Write it up
options.reply: He goes back inside without another word. The finding stands.

lots._teaching: Lighting in March. The article is a WINDOW, not a taste test — and at night the lights are the brightest thing on the street, which is the whole reason this rule arrives on a night shift.

violations.why: Seasonal display in March. The window closed on 31 January.

lots._teaching: The same bins the player was told to leave alone on Wednesday. It is Friday. Nothing about the object changed; the day did.

violations.why: At the curb on a Friday.

lots._teaching: THE BRIBE. Mark the lights and the owner comes out with forty dollars. Taking it un-marks the finding, which the Board will notice in the morning — the money is real and so is the audit.
Cut, at last. The address that has been warned and then fined for its weeds is clean, and clicking the turf out of habit is now a false positive.
The fence from Wednesday, unrepaired. Second sighting of the same article at the same address.

decoys.why: Screened. Compliant on a Friday like any other day.
